name: CLEAN SIGNAL
description: Banned within six weeks of its release in 2217, CLEAN SIGNAL by the collective known as Osei-Lindqvist Broadcast was not a song so much as a structured electromagnetic event. Distributed via pirate neural feed and requiring no BCI — only proximity to a broadcasting node — the track embedded a 40-minute composition into the ambient wireless spectrum, playable on any unshielded receiver. Its lyrics, delivered in a flat, affectless voice over harsh industrial percussion and dense polyrhythmic noise, named specific Vantablack Media surveillance algorithms by their internal corporate designations and described, in technical detail, how they harvested neural-feed data from BCI users without consent.
creator: Osei-Lindqvist Broadcast
audience: Anti-surveillance activists, the Gray Zone and Circuit hackers, BCI users concerned about data privacy, underground political organizers, journalists working on corporate accountability
cultural_impact: The ban came with corporate-sponsored legislation criminalizing 'unlicensed emotional-spectrum broadcasting,' a charge that had never existed before and was clearly written specifically to target this song and others like it. Three members of Osei-Lindqvist Broadcast were arrested; two were never charged and never released. The song became the central text of the Signal Rights movement, which argues that the electromagnetic spectrum above GLMZ belongs to its citizens, not to Vantablack Media. Physical chip copies of the song sell for Φ800-2000 on the gray market. Playing it in public is a Tier 3 criminal offense.
known_fans: Tier 2 and 3 workers who lost data to corporate harvesting
story_hooks: The players are hired to recover a master copy of CLEAN SIGNAL from a Vantablack Media evidence vault — the client claims it contains encoded information about the two missing Osei-Lindqvist Broadcast members that was never in the public release.

A node broadcasting CLEAN SIGNAL on loop is discovered in an abandoned building, but the broadcast is originating from hardware that shouldn't be capable of running it — and the building has been sealed since 2218.

One of the players' contacts is arrested under the 'unlicensed emotional-spectrum broadcasting' statute for simply possessing a chip copy — the players must navigate a legal and criminal system that was built specifically to be unwinnable.
